_doc: One row per surface material the course and terrain use. albedo/normal/weather are content.json ids; uv_scale is metres per texture tile. Course.gd draws every textured row with one weathering shader: weather is a second texture mixed in by noise over weather_cover of the surface, grime is the strength of dirt streaks running down from a ramp's top edge (and its chipped lip), detail is the close-up detail overlay that keeps the texture sharp under the player. filter: aniso = mipmapped anisotropic (every shader material samples this way since world_r1). panel: cast slab size in metres on ramp faces (dark joints, a tone per slab; 0 = none); tint: albedo multiplier; crease_ao: how much the foot of a ramp face (the valley crease) is darkened and occluded. leaks: strength of Rust's dirt_stains_leaks drip decals hanging from a ramp face's top edge; debris: strength of the same atlas's gravel/litter band along the foot of a face (the crease of a valley); course.json weathering says which atlas bands. 0 turns either off. normal_depth: strength of the normal map on the course shader (1 = as Rust ships it; higher deepens the slab seams, cracks and pitting under a low sun). color: a plain [r, g, b] albedo with no texture (the far ground ring), "(none)" for textured rows. seam_lock: panels per texture tile across u for a texture with cast panel seams baked in (the shader's second sampling then shifts whole panels so the seams never cross; 0 = free). panel_tone: tone spread from one cast panel strip to the next when seam_lock is set. weather_crop: share of the weather texture trimmed from each tile edge, for Rust textures drawn with a dark border round the tile. tile_crop_v: share of the base texture trimmed from its top and bottom edge (a slab texture's edge bevel), so the cast panels run on as long strips. ties is the strength of form-tie holes and the rust runs bled below some of them on ramp faces (course.json weathering tie_* / rust_*). specular: the shader's specular (Godot SPECULAR, 0.5 default): lower on concrete and tarmac so faces seen at grazing angles do not sheen pale (a look, unverified against Rust's own shader).
